Mesh Networking is a localized network backbone. Think of a city, let's call it Megacity One for giggles, where everybody is connected to everyone else. Each node acts as a server to the network; the physical topology of such a network bears a resemblance to the software driven structure of the Tor network. Because Tor functions within Layer 7 (application), it's redundancies are easily achieved - if one node fails, Tor just re-routes traffic. In order to achieve this effect in Layer 2 (data link) though, switches would have to be set up to enable most nodes to be connected to most other nodes. There's no larger internet, though. People connect to those servers locally, through local copper/fiber, using local routing or flooding

If Megacity One wanted to connect with Megacity 2, it would be stovepiped through direct connections between dedicated routers in M1 and M2.
